column1: # The SIMULATED counterpart to scripts/kmer_threshold_sweep.tsv, kept separate because it sets nothing:
# it is the evidence that simulated reads cannot derive the k-mer copy threshold, which is worth shipping
# because an earlier derivation rested on them and was wrong.
# Reads were simulated from three genomes at 0.2% substitution, no duplicates and no adapters, at depths
# from 5x to 400x, and each sample swept against the reference it came from.
# IMPORTANT: thresholds 1 to 20 only. The real sweep goes to 64. So where a plateau here reaches 20 it is
# censored at the edge of the measurement, not measured to its end -- do not read "to 20" as a finding.
# What is NOT censored, and is the point, is the LOWER edge: it stays at 3 or 4 at every depth from 50x to
# 400x, where real libraries of 420-535x need 32 copies before they reach their own plateau. Simulated
# reads therefore give no signal about where the threshold should sit.
# genome   the assembly the reads were simulated from
# copies   the -m value MASH was given
# shared   min-hashes shared with the source genome, of 1000
